findings.source_quote: αὗται αἱ ἐντολαὶ σύμφοροί εἰσι τοῖς μέλλουσι μετανοεῖν· ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ πορευθῶσιν ἐν αὐταῖς, εἰς μάτην ἐστὶν ἡ μετάνοια αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: These commandments help those who are ready to repent[a]. But if they do not live by them, their repentance is useless.
findings.issue: The preceding paragraph closes the speaker’s quotation, and this paragraph and the following exhortation have neither quotation marks nor renewed attribution. In the selected source, these remain the words of the figure speaking to Hermas. The punctuation instead presents them as unmarked narrator discourse.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the quotation open through the commandments and exhortation, ending it after “I have told you these things,” or explicitly identify these paragraphs as the same speaker’s continuing words. Review the resulting punctuation afresh.

findings.source_quote: πορεύεσθε οὖν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς μου ταύταις, καὶ ζήσεσθε τῷ Θεῷ.
findings.english_quote: Walk in these commandments of mine—follow them—and you will live as people devoted to God.
findings.issue: “Live as people devoted to God” recasts the assertion “you will live to God” as a description of devotion. It adds an explanatory characterization and obscures the source’s promise of life in relation to God.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “So follow these commandments of mine, and you will live for God.” Review this candidate against the force of ζήσεσθε τῷ Θεῷ before adoption; do not replace the life assertion with a claim solely about devoted conduct.

findings.source_quote: καὶ δεικνύει μοι ποιμένα νεανίσκον ἐνδεδυμένον σύνθεσιν ἱματίων, τῷ χρώματι κροκώδη.
findings.english_quote: The young man was wearing a saffron-colored garment with a varied design.
findings.issue: “With a varied design” adds a visual pattern not stated in the selected Greek. σύνθεσιν ἱματίων describes an ensemble or suit of clothing, not a patterned design; the English also reduces that ensemble to a single garment.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “The young man was wearing a saffron-colored outfit.” Review this candidate afresh for its representation of σύνθεσιν ἱματίων.

summary: The standard edition faithfully represents the supplied working source, including its difficult conditional assertions and negations. Its bracketed “[all]” retains the source’s distinction between bracketed material and unbracketed text. The simplified edition independently requires revision for an unsupported clothing detail, a recasting of the life assertion, and disrupted speaker attribution. Its omission of bracketed πάντα is not treated as loss of preserved text. Contextual repentance wording is compatible with current policy in both editions. This review evaluates the supplied text and disclosures, not unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation; proposed corrections require fresh review.
